name: Unreal Engine
description: Agents build your game in Unreal Editor 5.8 on this computer. Getting Unreal needs a free Epic account; each game has its own Unreal project. Unreal® is a trademark or registered trademark of Epic Games, Inc.

tools.name: use-project
tools.description: Link this game to an Unreal project: the one in this game's folder, or another the user asks for. Give its .uproject path, or the name the Unreal panel lists for a project already set up for Genex. A project that isn't set up yet is set up first, as the panel's Set up does, without asking: the chat shows the set-up and the link with one Undo that takes both back. When Unreal has that project open, Genex quits it first (Unreal asks about unsaved work itself), then opens it again. Later Unreal calls in this game go to that project. Switch to another project only when the user asks.

project.description: The project's .uproject path (any project; one not set up yet is set up first), or a set-up project's name (for example LanternPath).

tools.name: show-steps
tools.description: Show the user the Unreal setup card in this game's chat. On a computer without the Unreal Genex makes games with, it shows getting Epic's launcher and installing Unreal there (its Do it for me does both; the user signs in to Epic), and brings the Unreal button out; use it when the user wants an Unreal game and new-game refuses or the engine question says Unreal needs installing, then end your reply: the chat tells you when Unreal is installed. Otherwise it shows installing, updating or opening Xcode on a Mac, which lets you write C++ for this game; use it then when C++ would clearly help. On Windows it shows installing Microsoft's Visual Studio Build Tools, which packaging a game or plugin with C++ needs. It does nothing when every step is done.

tools.name: install-unreal
tools.description: Install what Unreal needs on this computer, one step per call, as Do it for me on the Unreal setup card does: Epic's launcher (on Windows Genex downloads it from Epic, checks Epic signed it and installs it; Windows asks the user for permission), then Unreal 5.8 in the launcher (Genex opens the launcher and hands the install to this chat's next turn, which clicks it with the desktop tool), then, on Windows when it is missing, Microsoft's Visual C++ runtime the editor needs, and, in a game with an Unreal project on Windows, Microsoft's Visual Studio Build Tools, which packaging C++ needs (Genex downloads Microsoft's installer, checks Microsoft signed it and installs them; Windows asks the user for permission): call it for them when a package says so. Call it yourself when the user wants an Unreal game and Unreal isn't installed, instead of asking them to install it; only signing in to Epic is theirs. It answers at once with what it started; end your reply then, and call it again for the next step once the card shows the last one done.

tools.name: new-game
tools.description: Make this game's Unreal project from one of Genex's Blueprint templates, in this game's folder as unreal/<name>.uproject: Genex sets it up, links this game to it and opens it in Unreal, as New game in the Unreal panel does. Use it only when the user chose Unreal Engine for this game and it has no Unreal project yet; a game folder that already has an unreal folder is refused. Unreal's first start takes minutes: Genex continues this chat by itself once Unreal is ready, so end your reply after this call with what you will build first.

template.description: TP_ThirdPersonBP (over-the-shoulder camera; walk, run and jump), TP_FirstPersonBP (from the player's eyes), TP_TopDownBP (camera high above; click where to go), TP_VehicleAdvBP (a sports car and an off-road buggy) or TP_BlankBP (an empty level).

variant.description: Optional. Combat, with TP_ThirdPersonBP only: Epic's Combat variant (a melee combo, enemies that fight back, a training arena), the base for a melee game. Leave it out for the template as it is.

name.description: The project's name: a letter first, then letters, digits or underscores, no spaces, at most 20 characters, such as LanternPath.

tools.name: new-plugin
tools.description: Make an Unreal C++ plugin in this game's folder: a host project unreal/<name>Host.uproject from Epic's Blank template (set up for Genex and linked to this game) with a C++ module of its own, and the plugin in unreal/Plugins/<name>/ from Epic's plugin template, enabled in the host. Use it only when the user wants an Unreal plugin (an editor tool, a window, a toolbar button, a runtime module) and this game has no Unreal project yet; a game folder that already has an unreal folder is refused. It opens nothing: build the plugin next.

name.description: The plugin's name: a letter first, then letters, digits or underscores, no spaces, at most 16 characters, such as LevelTools.

template.description: Optional. window (an editor tab with a menu entry and a toolbar button, the default), toolbar-button (a toolbar button that runs code) or blank (a runtime module with no editor parts).

tools.name: blueprint-guide
tools.description: Epic's own Blueprint guide and the full Blueprint text syntax (the (event …) and (fn …) forms a part's .dsl files use), read from this engine without Unreal. Read it before writing Blueprint text.

tools.name: find-nodes
tools.description: Look Blueprint node types up by a few words of their name in this engine's node reference, without Unreal: their exact type ids (the NodeType|Id a .dsl call names) and, where known, their pins. Pass the Blueprint's base and graph to see the nodes that context offers first.

query.description: Words of the node's name, such as "set intensity" or "print string".

base.description: Optional: the Blueprint's base class, such as Actor or Character.

tools.name: check-part
tools.description: Check a part you wrote in unreal/parts/<part>/ without Unreal: part.json, each Blueprint's text against this engine's nodes and the game's other parts, apply.py and test.json. Fix every problem it names and run it again until it passes; a part goes to the editor only once it does.

part.description: The part's name: its folder under unreal/parts.

tools.name: run-part
tools.description: For Genex's Unreal Loop only: put a part that passes check-part in the editor queue (apply, play its test, take play shots). Answers {id} at once; read part-result. Don't call it yourself in a chat.

part.description: The part's name: its folder under unreal/parts.

tools.name: part-result
tools.description: For Genex's Unreal Loop only: where a queued part run stands, with its play shots once done.

tools.name: rollback-part
tools.description: For Genex's Unreal Loop only: take a part's actors and its /Game/Parts folder out of the open editor before its files are restored.

part.description: The part's name: its folder under unreal/parts.

tools.name: reload-level
tools.description: For Genex's Unreal Loop only: reload the open level after a part's files were restored.

tools.name: export-reference
tools.description: For Genex's Unreal Loop only: export this engine's Blueprint node reference and Python names from the open editor, for check-part.

tools.name: cpp-status
tools.description: Whether this computer compiles Unreal C++, where Xcode (on a Mac) and Microsoft's C++ tools (on Windows) stand, and whether the game has its C++ module.

tools.name: add-cpp-module
tools.description: Add the game's C++ module, once the user confirms: Genex saves their open work in Unreal, then quits and reopens it in the background; after C++ changes call restart to rebuild. Answers {started} at once, or the module the game has; Genex starts this chat's next turn once it has ended, so you may end your turn meanwhile; cpp-status says how it went.
tools.confirmation: Add a C++ module to this Unreal game: Genex saves your open work in Unreal, then quits and reopens the editor in the background to build it.

tools.name: motion-status
tools.description: Whether the Game Animation Sample (Epic's Motion Matching characters) is among this Mac's Unreal projects, whether this game holds its content, and how adding it goes.

tools.name: add-motion-matching
tools.description: Add the Game Animation Sample's Motion Matching content to this game, once the user confirms: Genex saves their open work in Unreal, quits it, clones the sample's character, clips and pose databases into the game (kept out of its checkpoints), merges the sample's settings and plugins, and opens Unreal again; its first open takes about ten minutes. Needs the sample from Fab or the Epic Games Launcher among the user's Unreal projects. Answers {started} at once, or {already}; Genex starts this chat's next turn once it has ended, so you may end your turn meanwhile; motion-status says how it went. Then motion_character gives a character the sample's Motion Matching.
tools.confirmation: Add Epic's Game Animation Sample content (Motion Matching characters, about 2 GB, cloned from the sample on this Mac) to this Unreal game: Genex saves your open work in Unreal, quits it, adds the content and opens Unreal again; the first open takes about ten minutes.

tools.name: package-game
tools.description: Package this Unreal game as the app its players install: a Mac app on a Mac; on Windows, a Windows program, or a Linux one with system: "linux" (Unreal makes no Mac app off a Mac and no Windows app off Windows). A Linux package needs Epic's free Linux cross-compile toolchain for this Unreal: without it the call refuses with the installer's link, which you give the user, then package again once they ran it. Genex saves the open work in Unreal first (Unreal stays open), then runs Epic's BuildCookRun (Shipping) in the background into unreal/Builds/Mac/, unreal/Builds/Windows/ or unreal/Builds/Linux/, where Publish finds it. One package runs at a time per game. A first package compiles every shader and takes minutes. Answers {started, system} at once; Genex starts this chat's next turn once it has ended, so you may end your turn meanwhile; package-status (with the same system) says how it went. stop: true ends a running package.

stop.description: Optional. true ends the running package instead.

system.description: Optional. The system the app is for; this computer's own when left out. On Windows, "linux" packages a Linux app.

tools.name: package-status
tools.description: How this game's package for a system stands (system: "linux" for a Linux package on Windows; this computer's own system when left out): running, done (with the app's path inside the game and how long it took), failed (with its first error lines) or stopped; idle names an app already in that system's build folder.

system.description: Optional. The system the app is for; this computer's own when left out. On Windows, "linux" packages a Linux app.

tools.name: plugin-build
tools.description: Build this game's Unreal plugin with its host project, once the user confirms: Genex saves their open work in Unreal and quits it, then builds in the background and opens Unreal again after a good build (after a failed one it stays closed). Answers {started} at once; Genex starts this chat's next turn once it has ended, so you may end your turn meanwhile; plugin-status has the result and the errors to fix.

plugin.description: Optional. The plugin's folder name under unreal/Plugins/; needed only when the project holds more than one.

tools.confirmation: Build this Unreal plugin: Genex saves your open work in Unreal, quits it, builds the plugin in the background and opens Unreal again when the build passes.

tools.name: plugin-test
tools.description: Run the plugin's automation tests headless in the background (no window; Unreal can stay open). Tests whose names start with filter run (the plugin's name unless given). Answers {started, filter} at once; Genex starts this chat's next turn once it has ended, so you may end your turn meanwhile; plugin-status has passes, failures and the summary. stop: true ends a running test run.

plugin.description: Optional. The plugin's folder name under unreal/Plugins/; needed only when the project holds more than one.

filter.description: Optional. The start of the tests' names: letters, digits, _ and dots, such as LevelTools.Window.

stop.description: Optional. true ends the running test run instead.

tools.name: plugin-package
tools.description: Package the plugin for this computer (the Mac, or Win64 on Windows) with Epic's BuildPlugin in the background, into unreal/Saved/Genex/Packages/<Plugin>/ with a note beside it. Answers {started} at once; Genex starts this chat's next turn once it has ended, so you may end your turn meanwhile; plugin-status says how it went. stop: true ends a running package.

plugin.description: Optional. The plugin's folder name under unreal/Plugins/; needed only when the project holds more than one.

stop.description: Optional. true ends the running package instead.

tools.name: plugin-status
tools.description: How the plugin's build, tests and package stand (running, done, failed or stopped, with errors, test counts and failures), and proof: the paths of the test summary, the package note and the plugin window's picture, ready to name in finish.

plugin.description: Optional. The plugin's folder name under unreal/Plugins/; needed only when the project holds more than one.

tools.name: reopen-editor
tools.description: For Genex's Unreal Loop only: after Unreal crashed, reopen it in the background (end this game's hung editor and its crash reporter, build the game's C++ module, open the project and wait until it answers). Answers {started} at once, or {answering} when Unreal already answers; read editor-state.

tools.name: open-editor
tools.description: Open this game's Unreal project in Unreal; it starts in the background. Use it whenever an Unreal call says the project isn't open or isn't answering, or that Unreal crashed: it first ends what is left of a crashed editor of this project and its crash reporter. Answers {answering} when Unreal already answers, {starting} while Unreal is already opening it, {started} once Genex began opening it (then call editor-status with seconds until it answers; a first start takes minutes), or {busy} when its editor runs without answering: wait with editor-status, and only if it still doesn't answer call this again with restart: true, which ends that editor (work not saved in it is lost) and opens the project again.

restart.description: Optional. true ends this game's editor even while it runs without answering, then opens the project again; work not saved in it is lost.

tools.name: click-interface
tools.description: Click the game's own interface during a playtest (a menu drawn in C++ Slate, a button, a scoreboard: what the play's input and ui_press can't reach) with Genex's computer control: this chat's next turn may click inside Unreal Editor's game view with the desktop tool. With computer control off, Genex asks the person once on its card (Turn on computer control?), then macOS's own grants; call it yourself, never ask the person to turn it on. Say what in a few words. End your turn once it has started.

what.description: What to click and check, in a few words (at most 120 characters): open the team menu with M and pick Bravo.

tools.name: quit-editor
tools.description: Save every unsaved level and asset in this game's open Unreal (a play session is ended first), then quit it and its crash reporter. Use it when Unreal must be closed, or the user asks. It never quits an editor whose work it couldn't save, and says why. Open it again with open-editor. Answers {closed, ended}.

tools.name: editor-status
tools.description: Whether this game's Unreal answers, whether its editor process runs (null: can't tell), how Genex's opening of it goes (reopening: idle, reopening, done, or failed with its error) and where its Genex editor helper stands. With seconds (at most 170), it first waits up to that long for an opening to end. Call it after open-editor.

seconds.description: Optional. How long to wait for Unreal to answer or its opening to end; 0 or none only looks.

tools.name: editor-state
tools.description: For Genex's Unreal Loop only: whether this game's Unreal answers, and how reopening it goes.

tools.name: wait-editor
tools.description: For Genex's chat only: waits up to seconds (at most 170) for this game's own Unreal project to answer, and says where it stands: ready, starting, not-starting, port-blocked or no-project.

seconds.description: How long to wait; 0 only looks.

tools.name: engine-status
tools.description: For Genex's chat only: whether this computer has the Unreal Genex makes projects with (ready), only a newer one (newer-only), or none (none), and its version.

tools.name: play-check
tools.description: For Genex's Unreal Loop only: play the game in the editor as a checkpoint, applying nothing (settle, a shot where play starts, a drive along the route with frames, a shot after it, the board's checks, the probes). Answers {id} at once; read part-result.

checks.description: The board's checks by id: each {"tag": "genex:<name>", "exists": true or false} or {"player": a player_state field, "atLeast" and/or "atMost": a number}.

tools.name: save-all
tools.description: For Genex's Unreal Loop only: end a play session, then save every unsaved level and asset in this game's open editor.

tools.name: log-errors
tools.description: For Genex's Unreal Loop only: the error lines this game's editor log gained since an offset, without Unreal's own noise. Without since, where the log ends now.

since.description: The offset an earlier log-errors call answered.

tools.name: end-editor
tools.description: For Genex's Unreal Loop only: end this game's Unreal editor and its crash reporter, saving nothing (call save-all first).

tools.name: update-helper
tools.description: For Genex's Unreal Loop only: update this game's Genex editor helper to the plugin's while Unreal is closed; a helper file the user changed is kept beside it as .mine.

tools.name: editor-activity
tools.description: For Genex only: whether this game's open editor is in a play session (pie) and how many packages it holds unsaved (dirty), read before Genex saves its work; as the editor lock's probe, whether the person is using it (personActive: their play, not one the agent or Genex started) and how much is unsaved.

tools.name: hero-shots
tools.description: For Genex's Unreal Loop only: a still from each of the level's hero cameras whose labels start with prefix (GX_Shot_ unless given), at most max (8 unless given), each with its PNG data and tone numbers.

prefix.description: Optional: the start of the hero cameras' labels, GX_Shot_ unless given.

max.description: Optional: how many cameras to capture, 1 to 8 (8 unless given).

tools.name: play-open
tools.description: For Genex's computer tool only: start play in this game's editor (Play In Editor), or join the play already running. Answers {width, height, joined}, or {refused, message} (busy while the Loop plays a build, no-editor when Unreal is not open, unsupported for more than one player).

fresh.description: True: start the play over from the game's start (a play an agent left running is ended first; the person's is never touched).

tools.name: play-input
tools.description: For Genex's computer tool only: move the player's mouse for one frame when asked, then hold keys together for seconds of the game's own time, then let go. Answers {held, gameSeconds} once that time has passed, or {refused, message}.

keys.description: Web key codes or mouse buttons (MouseLeft, MouseRight, MouseMiddle) held together, joined by commas: KeyW,ShiftLeft (empty: just let the game play).

seconds.description: Game seconds to hold them, 0.05 to 10.

dx.description: Pixels of mouse motion to the right for one frame first (negative: left).

dy.description: Pixels of mouse motion down the screen for one frame first (negative: up).

wheel.description: Notches of the mouse wheel for one frame first, up positive.

tools.name: play-shot
tools.description: For Genex's computer tool only: a picture of what the player sees in the running play (no on-screen UI). Answers {data (base64), mime (image/png), png (the same data), width, height}, or {refused, message}.

tools.name: play-state
tools.description: For Genex's computer tool only: the player in the running play (player_state: pawn, location, speed, game seconds, and the findings its bug detectors told since the last read), or {refused, message}.

tools.name: play-pause
tools.description: For Genex's computer tool only: stand the running play still (paused true) or let it run (paused false), as its own pause does. Answers {paused}, or {refused, message}.

paused.description: True stands the game still; false lets it run.

tools.name: play-close
tools.description: For Genex's computer tool only: end the play the computer started (a play the person or the Loop started goes on) and give Unreal's background throttle back. Answers {closed}.

tools.name: play-walk
tools.description: For Genex's computer tool only: walk the player to a target by itself (the level's nav mesh, else straight; never off a drop; it jumps, side-steps and plans again when blocked) and answer once the walk has ended: {state: arrived|stuck|stopped|timed-out|failed, target, way, partial, distanceM, tried, reason, gameSeconds}, or {refused, message}.

target.description: An actor's label or name (or part of it), or x,y,z in cm.

seconds.description: The most game seconds the walk may take (default 20, at most 120).

tools.name: play-look
tools.description: For Genex's computer tool only: turn the player's view onto a target with the mouse and answer once the turn has ended: {state: looked|stopped|timed-out|failed, target, offDegrees, reason, gameSeconds}, or {refused, message}.

target.description: An actor's label or name (or part of it), or x,y,z in cm.

tools.name: play-pilot
tools.description: For Genex's computer tool only: start a pilot, a file of the project that plays toward one goal by itself every frame, choosing among the moves it names; answers at once: {piloting, pilot, seconds, decide, stages}, {error} with the file's line, or {refused, message}.

file.description: The pilot's .py file: in the game folder's pilots/ (pilots/<goal>.py), or relative to the Unreal project.

seconds.description: The most game seconds it may play, up to 300.

decide.description: Put each decision out as an ask for Genex's fast decision model; false picks by the pilot's order.

tools.name: play-pilot-step
tools.description: For Genex's computer tool only: one step of the running pilot, handing it the answer to its ask or stopping it: {phase: piloting, ask, applied, running, stage, byOrder, gameSeconds} or {phase: over, report}.

answer.description: JSON {id, probabilities, answers, ms} for the ask with that id.

tools.name: open-for-run
tools.description: For Genex only: at a run's start, make sure this game's Unreal is open with the current Genex editor helper and its reference exported.

skills.name: unreal-editor
skills.summary: How to build this Unreal game in the person's open editor: the unreal-editor toolsets, linking the project with use-project, Blueprints (guides and node lookups first), C++, play-testing with the computer tool, saving and checkpoints.

skills.name: unreal-plugin
skills.summary: How to ship this Unreal plugin from its host project: plugin-build, automation tests and plugin-test, then plugin-package, reading plugin-status between steps.

actions.name: setup
actions.label: Set up project
actions.confirmation: Set up this Unreal project for Genex: turn on Epic's MCP plugins and toolsets in its .uproject, start the MCP server on the project's own port when it opens, and add the Genex editor helper to its Plugins folder. Genex keeps a copy of each file first.

actions.name: undo-setup
actions.label: Undo setup
actions.confirmation: Take back what Genex added to this Unreal project: its plugin entries, the MCP server start-up lines and the Genex editor helper. Anything else you changed stays.

actions.name: ray-tracing-off
actions.label: Turn off ray tracing
actions.confirmation: Turn off hardware ray tracing in this Unreal project: Genex sets r.RayTracing=False in its Config/DefaultEngine.ini. On a Mac, Unreal 5.8 can crash while it renders a ray-traced game behind another app. Lumen keeps lighting the level in software, and you can turn ray tracing back on in Project Settings.

actions.name: agents
actions.label: Whether agents may use Unreal while you play

actions.name: agents-go-ahead
actions.label: Let agents use Unreal while you play

actions.name: agents-wait
actions.label: Have agents wait while you play

mcpServers.description: The user's open Unreal Editor 5.8 through Epic's Unreal MCP on 127.0.0.1. Set up Unreal prepares a project: Epic's MCP plugins on, the server starting on a port of the project's own, and the Genex editor helper. Each game's calls go to the Unreal project Genex linked it to; a game without one uses the project chosen in the panel.

workerTypes.description: Writes C++ in a copy and checks it with the plugin's sandboxed build

folders.why: Unreal's build tool writes its log here
.NET keeps the build tool's configuration lock here
